# `Q-13-19` — Invalid toc-expand value

> The `toc-expand` option has a value Quarto cannot use. The table
> of contents opens to the default depth of 1.

## What this means

`toc-expand` sets how much of the table of contents is open when
the page loads (see [Following the reader](../../guides/authoring/navigation.qmd#following-the-reader)).
It accepts:

| value | behavior |
|---|---|
| `true` | every entry is always open |
| `false` (or `0`) | nested entries open only while their section is current |
| a number `N` of 1 or more | entries down to level `N` stay open |

A number with a fractional part is rounded down: `2.5` behaves like
`2`. Any other value is ignored, and this warning names it. The
document still renders, and the table of contents behaves as if
`toc-expand` were not set.

## Why this happens

- **A word instead of a number or boolean**, such as `all`, `none`,
  or `deep`.
- **A negative depth**, such as `-2`.

## How to fix

Use `true` to open everything, `false` to keep nested entries
closed, or a depth such as `2`. Remove the option to get the
default.
